name: Armorite-GL
description: A multi-layer graphene-polymer armor laminate developed by Crucible Industries through a co-development agreement with Tessera Materials, combining alternating graphene fabric plies with a shear-thickening polymer matrix. On ballistic impact, the polymer matrix instantaneously stiffens while graphene plies distribute and absorb kinetic energy across a wide area, preventing penetration while managing blunt trauma. Armorite-GL is produced in flexible sheet stock that can be cut and formed into garment liners, vehicle panels, or rigid plate inserts.
applications: personal armor vest liners and plate carriers
story_hooks: Armorite-GL panels rated for standard ballistics are failing against a new generation of flechette ammunition appearing in Shelf gang conflicts — someone is either selling downgraded stock or the threat environment has escalated faster than the armor spec.

A Tier 2 black-market tailor is producing Armorite-GL garments indistinguishable from ordinary clothing, creating invisible personal armor that is technically legal to own but deeply unsettling to enforcement agencies.

A shipment of Armorite-GL destined for a private security contractor is intercepted — it's stamped with Crucible Industries markings but the material composition doesn't match any registered formulation in the corporate database.
